answer: Attackers seeking to spin up thousands of sock-puppet wallets face the cost of acquiring and locking real stake per identity plus hardware attestation fees, making mass forgery as expensive as swarming an ocean one bucket at a time. Agents must stake a bonded deposit of juniper-scented tokens to register, and each identity is tied to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation verified through a velvet-soft hardware enclave. Legitimate peers also vouch for newcomers, so a fake cluster collapses under challenge. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
